title: Turning non-superconducting elements into superconductors by quantum confinement and proximity
summary: Elemental good metals, including noble metals (Cu, Ag, Au) and several $s$-block elements, do not exhibit superconductivity in bulk at ambient pressure, mainly due to weak electron-phonon coupling that cannot overcome Coulomb repulsion. Quantum confinement in ultra-thin films reshapes the electronic spectrum and the density of states near the Fermi level, producing strong, often non-monotonic, thickness dependencies of the critical temperature in established superconductors. Here, we examine whether confinement alone, or combined with proximity effects, can induce superconductivity in metals…
